2026-07-07-first-trail-marathon.text:
Finally crossed the finish line of my first official trail marathon and I’m genuinely proud of myself.

A few months ago, even running 5K on flat road felt challenging. Then one day I started running out of curiosity but somewhere along the way that curiosity turned into habit and eventually, into something I genuinely enjoy.

Last day, I finished 26th out of 213 runners. Maybe it’s not an extraordinary result for someone, but it means a lot for me. Bc I had only been running for short time and besides, this wasn’t an ordinary road race. It was trail marathon, taking us through mountains, endless climbs, rocky paths, steep descents, and hundreds of stairs by rainy day.
That’s why I’m happy with how my body responded. Bc the biggest victory wasn’t my finishing position, it was realizing how much my endurance has improved. Every evening run and every kilometer I trained for was worth it. So it showed me once again that consistency really does pay off. 

Now I’m looking forward to what comes next, because there are much bigger races waiting ahead and I’ll keep challenging myself.

So, see you at the next starting line…..

2026-11-16-lumi-understands-like-a-human.text:
Lumi understands like a human 📍

This is Jaka Lumi, a wheeled mobile manipulator developed by JAKA Robotics  as an embodied AI platform. It combines a mobile base with lidar-based navigation, lifting column, rotating waist, two-axis head and a six-axis JAKA collaborative arm with gripper, giving it 12 degrees of freedom in total. For perception it uses two RGB-D cameras and microphone array and its onboard AI computing runs on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor. 

You can find more hardware details here: https://lnkd.in/gftqYdEP

What if you could simply tell a robot what you need, the same way you would ask a colleague?

That is what I'm building with Lumi. I gave Lumi ordinary spoken requests with no fixed commands, no special phrasing. But it understood and acted on them.

The system is built as a pipeline of several AI components, all running on the robot's onboard computer. ASR transcribes the speech into text. An LLM interprets the intent of each request, including short and informal phrasing and translates it into executable tasks for the mobile base, the body and the arm. TTS provides spoken feedback, allowing the robot to confirm its actions during the interaction. 

In parallel, The CV system working with the depth cameras provides spatial awareness. It detects people and objects, estimates their position and distance relative  to the robot and identifies attributes such as colour and shape. This information allows language-based instructions to be grounded in the robot's physical environment. 

Running the entire system locally was a deliberate design decision. It reduces response latency, keeps all audio and visual data on the device and allows the  robot to operate independently of network availability.

This is only the first step. There is much more to learn and I will keep sharing as Lumi grows.

#robotics #mobilerobot #jakarobtics
